S01.institution: British Museum via Google Arts & Culture
S01.artifact: 1989,0130.4, Late Uruk, The first writing: counting beer for the workers
S01.locator: Object description paragraphs 1–4 and Details: date, registration number, period/culture

approved_tests.limit: Earlier test copy; not the new segment narration or approved historical script

panels.title: PAYDAY
panels.narration: Your payday arrives. It is a jar. Excellent liquidity.

action.start: The crow braces to receive a neat modern envelope, an overt present-day metaphor.
action.resolution: An oversized beer jar pops out instead; the crow nearly buckles, then steadies it on the counter.

panels.comic_expression: Wide-eyed surprise becomes an absurdly professional nod.

panels.title: SMALL PRINT
panels.narration: A paycheck? Easy. Proving history’s first? Less easy.

action.start: The crow starts to celebrate the jar.
action.resolution: A giant question mark drawn in post drops between crow and jar; celebration freezes.

panels.comic_expression: One eyebrow snaps upward; the wing slowly lowers.

panels.title: MESOPOTAMIA
panels.narration: Mesopotamia. More than five thousand years ago. Bring a cup.

action.start: A simple 2D backdrop unfolds behind the crow.
action.resolution: The crow produces an absurdly tiny cup beside the giant jar and stares at the mismatch.

panels.comic_expression: Deadpan scale comparison; no historical quantity is implied.

panels.title: THE RECEIPT
panels.narration: This British Museum tablet records beer allocated to workers.

action.start: The crow dramatically gestures toward an illustrative clay prop.
action.resolution: The prop lands on the counter; the crow checks its balance instead of striking a solemn museum pose.

panels.comic_expression: The grand reveal ends with a practical little adjustment.

panels.title: RATIONS
panels.narration: Daily rations, specifically. Civilization brought its own paperwork.

action.start: The jar and illustrative tablet sit separately on the counter.
action.resolution: The crow slides the tablet beside the jar, then recoils from the resulting paperwork pile.

panels.comic_expression: Dry bureaucratic exasperation; the extra props are a comic metaphor.

panels.title: THE DATE
panels.narration: Between thirty-one hundred and three thousand BC, says the museum.

action.start: A program-drawn date card enters beside the crow.
action.resolution: The crow tries to straighten the card; it tilts the other way, then finally settles.

panels.comic_expression: A serious fact delivered during a petty fight with the caption.

panels.title: KEEP THE RECEIPT
panels.narration: That is a very long time to keep receipts.

action.start: The crow carefully files the illustrative tablet.
action.resolution: The filing slot is far too small; the crow measures the tablet with a wing, unimpressed.

panels.comic_expression: One unhurried blink after a quick failed attempt.

panels.title: A JAR SIGN
panels.narration: The beer sign represents a jar. Branding: aggressively literal.

action.start: The crow points at a blank diagram area, not at invented glyphs on the prop.
action.resolution: A program-drawn jar diagram is revealed and explicitly captioned as a schematic.

panels.comic_expression: The crow looks from jar to diagram and gives a tiny exhausted nod.

panels.title: CONTENTS INCLUDED
panels.narration: Its wavy lines show beer inside. Helpful accounting.

action.start: The diagram remains fixed while its interior is empty.
action.resolution: The program reveals schematic waves; the crow leans in, then theatrically grasps the obvious.

panels.comic_expression: An exaggerated recognition reaction; no claim of an exact transcription.

panels.title: THREE SIGNS
panels.narration: The sign appears three times. Count symbols, not drinks.

action.start: Three schematic icons appear individually, drawn by the program.
action.resolution: The crow counts them with wing beats and stops a comic fourth icon before it lands.

panels.comic_expression: A rapid correction, not a drinking action or a consumption claim.

panels.title: BOWL AND HEAD
panels.narration: Another sign connects a bowl and a human head.

action.start: An isolated explanatory diagram panel replaces the jar schematic.
action.resolution: A program-drawn bowl and head diagram move together; the crow tracks the join with an exaggerated head turn.

panels.comic_expression: A visual explanation with a reaction; the head is a diagram, not a new speaking character.

panels.title: READ THE RECORD
panels.narration: It means eating. We are reading a ration record.

action.start: The explanatory symbols are separated on a blank area.
action.resolution: They align beside a program-drawn RATIONS label; the crow accepts the conclusion with an overformal bow.

panels.comic_expression: An overly grand bow for a mundane administrative discovery.

panels.title: NO FIRST PRIZE
panels.narration: A record, not proof of humanity’s very first wage.

action.start: The crow is offered a comic FIRST trophy graphic.
action.resolution: The crow pushes it back and points to the actual source reference instead.

panels.comic_expression: Celebration denied by the evidence, with a perfectly straight face.

panels.title: NO MAGIC NUMBER
panels.narration: No universal litres per worker can be read from that.

action.start: An unsupported numerical badge tries to enter the frame.
action.resolution: The crow blocks the blank badge with a wing before any number appears; only the source citation remains.

panels.comic_expression: A firm librarian stare; no invented ration appears even as a gag.

panels.title: BEER AND BUREAUCRACY
panels.narration: Beer. Workers. Paperwork. The real story is already absurd enough.

action.start: The crow arranges the jar and illustrative record into a tidy final composition.
action.resolution: The jar is placed safely, the tablet stack wobbles, and the crow catches it while keeping the golden signature tablet in the beak.

panels.comic_expression: A quick physical payoff followed by a deadpan stare into camera.

production_trials.animation_limit: Fifteen new expressive illustrated poses, timed editorial cuts, compositor camera/dust and program-drawn diagrams; no claim of continuous articulated character animation
